the functional status of the human follicles was correlated with the microvascular bed, with the epithelial expression pattern of newly discovered proteins, and with the colloid content of Tg-I. Titolo: Structural and molecular changes in the human thyroid gland.

(1) active follicles are larger than hypofunctioning ones, (2) the capillary network is larger and more complex around active follicles, (3) VEGF is detected at the basal pole in multinodular goiter follicles, and (4) hypofunctioning thyrocytes do not express TPO, ThOXs, pendrin and do not contain Tg-I.
the functional status of follicles is related to the expression of iodine transport and organization proteins in the epithelium, and is associated with changes in the capillary bed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional status of follicles in human thyroids and the vascularization of the follicles.
the structural and molecular changes occurring between active and hypotrophic follicles, in normal and pathological thyroids.
the functional status of thyroid follicles and the microvasculature in contact with them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thyroid gland of humans and other mammals is made of angiofolli- cular units, which may be active or hypofunctioning.
the angiofollocular unit is the functional unit of the thyroid gland.
the angiofolli-cular units are present in both active and hypofunctio-ning follicles in the human thyroid gland.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the epithelial expression pattern of proteins involved in the iodine transport and organization is related to the functional state of the follicles, and the microvascular bed is a key component for the functional state of thyroid follicles.

the functional status of thyroid follicular cells is related to the presence or absence of the following proteins: TSH receptor, Tg-I, pendrin, Na(+)/ I(-) symporter and TPO, and that these proteins are related to the presence of the vascular network.
the thyroid gland is not a simple gland, but a gland with different compartments, each of them with a specific function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of pendrin, TSH receptor, and Tg in the human thyroid is related to the iodination capacity of thyrocyte.
the epithelial expression patterns of the proteins involved in iodide transport and organification are in agreement with the functional status of follicles.

the epithelial expression pattern of newly identified proteins involved in iodide transport and organification, such as pendrin and ThOXs, can be used to distinguish hypofunctioning and active human thyroid follicles.
